name: NJ CSO Group 'Combined Sewer Overflow Notification System (interim)' (njcsonotifications.com)
operator: NJ CSO Group (permittees coordinated by Passaic Valley Sewerage Commission; site does not name its operator or developer)
event_types: cso_likely (rainfall-threshold estimate, not an observed discharge)
waters_covered: 15 CSO permits: East Newark, Fort Lee, Bayonne, Elizabeth, Hackensack, Newark, Paterson, Perth Amboy, Jersey City MUA, North Bergen MUA Central and Woodcliff, Guttenberg, Harrison, Kearny, Ridgefield Park. Status is per permittee (whole municipality), not per outfall or water.
access_detail: Server-rendered page plus undocumented JSON: GET https://njcsonotifications.com/?handler=Status (no auth; JSON; page polls it every 300 s per its live-status-settings). Same JSON is embedded in the page as <script id='permittee-status-data'>. Old URL https://njcso.hdrgateway.com/ now shows 'This site has moved' and redirects after 15 s. A 'past conditions' view is mentioned on /About but no query parameter was found (asOf=, at=, date= ignored). Fetched 2026-11-02 17:53 UTC: 0 of 15 'likely'.
fills_event_fields: source_updated_at (lastUpdatedLabel, local time label without year)
cadence: Hourly precipitation (Iowa Environmental Mesonet gridded estimates for a representative point per permittee); page re-polls every 5 min. The site says permittees are marked as having no current data if the update is more than a couple of hours old.
history: No archive found. Must be polled and stored by us.
license: No terms found on the site. Footer: '© 2026 NJ Combined Sewer Overflow Notification System'. Site says: 'This site indicates when an overflow is likely, not that one has occurred.' and 'is not a substitute for official notifications from a permit holder or from the New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection.'
legal_basis: NJPDES CSO permits Part IV.F.8.b.iii: 'The permittee shall maintain on a daily basis a CSO Notification System website to inform interested citizens of CSO discharges that are occurring or have occurred.'
status_reason: The only shared, machine-readable NJ CSO status feed. But it is a rainfall model per municipality, labelled interim, and its predecessor was down for part of 2026 (Elizabeth's Aug 1 2026 progress report: 'The website is currently down.'). Usable as a 'CSO likely' advisory layer, never as a confirmed discharge.
notes: Labels: 'CSO event unlikely' (alertLevel 1); other levels not observed on a dry day. About page: 'a CSO event is reported as becoming more likely, and then as likely to be occurring.' Times are Eastern. Not covered: NHSA (Hoboken etc.), Camden City, Gloucester City, CCMUA, Trenton. Raw: raw/njcsonotif-home.html, raw/njcsonotif-about.html, raw/njcso-status-20261102.json.

name: Old NJ CSO Notification System at njcso.hdrgateway.com (HDR-hosted, 2016-2026)
access_detail: Fetched: now a 'This site has moved' page with meta refresh to https://njcsonotifications.com/ ('This site is being migrated to a new URL').

PVSC LTCP site: 'uses real time radar-based rainfall measurements and model-derived rating curves to assess the likelihood of a CSO event.'

name: NJDEP Hotline 1-877-WARN-DEP (1-877-927-6337) - mandatory noncompliance and dry-weather overflow reports
access_detail: Reporting line for permittees and the public. No public log, map or feed of calls found. Individual complaint/intake records surface only through OPRA requests (e.g. Jersey Shore Online, 2026-10-30, quoting a DEP intake record for a May 31 sewage release in Barnegat).
cadence: Within 2 hours (N.J.A.C. 7:14A-6.10(c)) or 24 hours (6.10(d)) of the event or of awareness; written report within 5 days (6.10(e)).
legal_basis: N.J.A.C. 7:14A-6.10; NJPDES CSO permits Part IV.F.5.b (dry weather overflows must be reported under 6.10(c) and (e)).
status_reason: Not public. The reports exist but go to DEP only; the owner could ask NJDEP (or file OPRA) for a periodic export of sewage-related hotline incidents.
notes: Every CSO outfall sign must say 'Report dry weather discharge to NJDEP Hotline at 1 (877) 927-6337 (WARN-DEP).'

sample_record.Part IV.F.8.b.iii: The permittee shall maintain on a daily basis a CSO Notification System website to inform interested citizens of CSO discharges that are occurring or have occurred.
sample_record.Part IV.C.1.d: The permittee shall report Duration of Discharge on the MRF for each CSO outfall as a whole day for any calendar day when a discharge occurs.

legal_basis: N.J.A.C. 7:14A; N.J.A.C. 7:14A-11.12 (Federal CSO Policy, Appendix C)
status_reason: The legal basis for NJ CSO notification: signs, leaflets, annual mailing, and a daily-maintained notification website. No deadline in hours for public notice.
notes: Original 2015 permits (effective 2015-07-01): signs by January 2016 and a hotline or website by July 1, 2016 (per Jersey Water Works 2016 and Water Online 2016; permit text not read). Renewals also require LTCP 'Post Construction Compliance Monitoring Program' with 'A Public Notification System to notify the public of the occurrence of combined sewer overflows for each receiving water body' (Part IV.G, Camden permit).

access_detail: Fetched. Full text: 'Permits issued for discharges from combined sewer overflows shall include applicable provisions of the Federal Combined Sewer Overflow (CSO) Policy (59 Federal Register 18688, published April 19, 1994) incorporated herein at Appendix C.'
status_reason: Makes NMC #8 (public notification) a permit requirement; sets no timing.

name: New Jersey CSO public-notification bills (S3119/A4380 2010-11; S831 2012-13; A2908 2018-19) and search for 2024-2026 bills
access_detail: LegiScan answered 403 to curl. Facts from search snippets: S831 (2012-13) passed both houses and was not signed by Gov. Christie (pocket veto, Jan 2014); it would have required DEP to alert the public within 24 hours of a permittee's report. A2908 (2018-19) 'would establish notification, signage, and monitoring requirements related to combined sewer overflows' (introduced only). No 2024-2025 or 2026-2027 NJ bill on sewage or CSO public notification was found in two searches.
status_reason: No statute requires public notice of CSOs or SSOs in NJ; the requirement lives only in NJPDES permits.
notes: An enacted law would change the 'when was notice due' logic; re-check njleg.state.nj.us bill search directly (not reachable from here via LegiScan).

name: EPA ECHO Effluent Charts REST (NJ CSO outfall DMRs: 'Duration of discharge' days per month, precipitation, solids/floatables)
operator: US EPA (data reported by permittees to NJDEP and passed to ICIS-NPDES)
event_types: cso (monthly count of discharge days per outfall)
waters_covered: All NJ CSO permits in ICIS (tested 9: Newark, JCMUA, Camden City, Paterson, Bayonne, Gloucester City, NHSA Adams St, Trenton, plus PVSC DFR)
access_detail: No key. Parameter 81381 'Duration of discharge', unit 'd', statistical base 'MO TOTAL' per CSO outfall (feature type EXO); outfall 002 of each permit also carries 00193 precipitation and 51892 solids/floatables. Trimmed results: raw/echo/cso-dmr-days-trimmed.json.
cannot_fill: volume (not reported in NJ CSO DMRs)
cadence: Monthly. Received 16-27 days after month end at most permittees (median), but Newark 36-146 days (median 97); Gloucester City 0-13. Latest period on 2026-11-02: Aug or Sep 2026.
legal_basis: NJPDES CSO permits Part IV.C.1.d ('as a whole day for any calendar day when a discharge occurs'); values are modeled for most permittees (Part IV.A.1.c allows a DEP-approved model).
status_reason: Best historical, machine-readable record of NJ CSO activity per outfall. Monthly and modeled, so it is a history/statistics layer, not a notice feed.
notes: Data quality: Bayonne's May-25 and Jul-25 rows are identical; Bayonne 001 reports 17-26 days a month. 2025 May had 11-15 discharge days at many JCMUA/Camden/Newark outfalls.

Fetched: public/beaches/statuses/ (status codes), public/beaches/statuses/legend (counts by program), public/data/filters (programs, 21 counties, 565 municipalities, 31 local health authorities, beachList of 1,600 stations with lat/lon), public/lhas/, public/geography, public/data/counts?startDate=&endDate=. Other public routes seen: public/snapshots/, public/dailyFlights/, public/news/, public/photos/, public/faqs/. https://www.njbeaches.org has a certificate name mismatch; https://njbeaches.org works.
cadence: In season (mid-May to mid-Sept): ocean/bay sampled weekly on Mondays (incident start dates fall on sample day), retest next day; status changes posted daily. On 2026-11-02 all 499 stations were 'not yet open / closed for season'.
history: 2025: 201 incidents; 2026: 409 incidents (2025 CCMP rows look sparse: 27). Water-quality download by date range; counts endpoint gives totals (e.g. July 2025: 2,211 results, 87 incidents).
license: No terms found on njbeaches.org or in the API. NJDEP is the publisher; credit 'NJDEP Cooperative Coastal Monitoring Program'.

status_reason: Best NJ feed to build against: open JSON/CSV, coordinates, daily in season, and it codes sewage-related actions (Beach_Source_Type 'CSO', indicator 'PREEMPT').
